content: MK's survey finds three themes in Ṣāʾin al-Dīn's image in late Timurid Herat: his close relationship to Sharaf al-Dīn Yazdī, fellow disciple of Sayyid Ḥusayn Akhlāṭī in Cairo; his status as Sayyid Ḥusayn's chief disciple and so Sharaf al-Dīn's own teacher; and the pair as the two most prominent intellectuals of Shahrukhid Iran. MK reads this as consistent with Ṣāʾin al-Dīn's self-presentation as expounder of Akhlāṭī's teaching and as showing that, his personal tribulations notwithstanding, the Isfahan Circle's project was held in wide esteem.
refers_to_primary: MK's survey of late 9th/15th and early 10th/16th-century biographical sources
